learning_robustness.title: Learning under input corruption
learning_robustness.alt: Test accuracy for MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and KMNIST as training pixel-replacement noise increases, with example corrupted images below each plot.
learning_robustness.short: Neural networks retain substantial predictive power well above chance, even when trained on heavily corrupted images.
learning_robustness.caption: Width-128, three-layer ReLU networks trained with cross-entropy on corrupted inputs and intact labels, evaluated on clean test images. The curves average 100 noisy training realizations; shaded bands show one standard deviation. Dashed lines mark chance accuracy.

learning_theory.title: Testing the high-noise centroid theory
learning_theory.alt: Comparison of ensemble-mean network accuracy with fitted centroid-model predictions, with insets comparing output values for three datasets.
learning_theory.short: A controlled comparison between the centroid response and network experiments.
learning_theory.caption: Controlled theory validation uses width-2048, three-layer erf networks trained with mean squared error, distinct from the ReLU/cross-entropy experiments above. The dashed curve is a fitted effective model; the insets compare individual output values at 97% replacement noise. Accuracy error bars show one standard deviation.

quantum_classification.title: Classifying monitored quantum dynamics
quantum_classification.alt: Diagram connecting many-body evolution operators and single-particle transfer matrices to symmetry classes and topological classifications through a dynamical bulk-boundary correspondence.
quantum_classification.short: Two complementary descriptions connect symmetry, topology, and the states produced by monitored dynamics.
quantum_classification.caption: The many-body evolution-operator and single-particle transfer-matrix descriptions lead to corresponding classifications in the free-fermion limit. A dynamical bulk–boundary correspondence connects spacetime topology to the topology of the steady-state ensemble.

quantum_protocol.title: Adaptive topological-state preparation
quantum_protocol.alt: Adaptive circuit with physical and ancillary lattices, localized-mode measurements, outcome-dependent corrections, and redistribution of ancillary particles.
quantum_protocol.short: Measurements and feedforward steer the physical system toward topological states.
quantum_protocol.caption: Each cycle measures localized modes in the physical system, applies corrections conditioned on the outcomes, and redistributes ancillary particles. The construction connects a topological classification to a concrete measurement-feedback protocol.
